inconsistencies: Chain: #36554 (reject warnings in flag checks, -msse4.1 for SHA-NI) is a stated prerequisite for #31507 (clang-cl Windows); review #36554 first even though #31507 carries the larger benefit.
Chain: #36531 (guix --load-path) is the base of both #25573 (-static-pie) and #36193 (--disable-wchar_t); it must land first or those two cannot be evaluated.
Chain: #36509 removes dead code and enables -Wunused-macros/-Wunused-template specifically to unblock #36167 (-Wunused); review #36509 first.

Toolchain-baseline set: #36042 (g++ 13), #36036 (clang 19) and #36287 (Xcode CLT 26.3) are one transition feeding #36033 (C++23 RFC). They were originally scored 17, 33 and 12 despite being the same decision; they now share a band, and #36033 should not be decided before them.

Overlapping family: #36167 (-Wunused), #36268 (-Wextra-semi), #35911 (-Wmissing-noreturn) and #36509 all enable compiler warning flags plus a mechanical cleanup. #36167 is the broadest and should set the precedent; the others should follow its outcome rather than be reviewed independently.
Overlapping area: #35722 (cache BSD SDK sources) and #36147 (native BSD CI jobs) both reshape BSD CI. #36147 is the substantive one; #35722 may be moot if #36147 changes how BSD jobs are provisioned.

Overlapping area: #35197 (--icf=safe on darwin), #36193 (--disable-wchar_t) and #36269 (_GLIBCXX_USE_DEPRECATED=0) are all Guix binary-size trims by the same author; they should be judged as one group, with #35197 and #36193 clearly above #36269 (bytes only).

IPC build cluster: #19460, #32387, #36060, #36556 and #35068 all touch the multiprocess/capnproto build path. #35068 (depends CMake package discovery) and #36060 (KJ exception check) fix configure-time breakage and should be reviewed ahead of the feature-side #19460 and #32387.

Release-integrity cluster: #36534 (hardening flags) and #36293 (verification quorum) were both scored P2 while #36531 and #35765 were P1, although all four decide whether a correct, hardened, verifiable binary ships; they are now banded together.
result.notes: Band spread used deliberately: four P1s all concern whether a correct and hardened release binary is produced or verified; P2 holds durable platform/CI/toolchain work; the long P3 tail is ordered so that fixes for actual build failures (#36106, #35068) sit above preventive CI coverage, which sits above size and warning cleanups. Draft, RFC and stale-rebase status was ignored throughout (#36033, #35356, #36270, #36060, #35167).
